clue.text: Happen in company encountered on way from Paris

parts.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them
rue is the French word for a street, a way in Paris

explanation.surface: Something happens while a group meets on the road out of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To come about or be realised, as a wish or prediction does, is a two-word phrasal equivalent of happen.

clue.text: Ruler initially used in producing triangle, square and rectangle

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A ruler is a drawing tool used to produce geometric shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' looks like the drawing instrument from the geometry picture; it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor of Russia was a monarch, so the title names a kind of sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Spears and bows

definitions.meaning: spears as a verb: pierces with a point
violin bows are wooden ... strung with horsehair

explanation.surface: Weapons of an ancient army: spears and bows.
explanation.definitionFit: Piercing with a point is one sense, and slender rods such as a fiddler's bows are the other.

clue.text: Cover up work of 22 across that's problematic

definitions.note: a noun phrase sense: something that is a quandary

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for the cover is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen, the answer to 22 across

explanation.surface: Hiding a novelist's work sounds like a tricky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LID to DIL, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary between two awkward choices is by nature a situation that is problematic.

clue.text: Cause of illness in kind of camel endlessly needing drug injected

indicators.note: injected means the drug's letter is put inside the trimmed camel word
endlessly means the final letter of the camel word is cut off

parts.note: the Bactrian is the two-humped camel
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sick camel needs a drug injecting to fight infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BACTRIAN to BACTRIA, and 'injected' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Microbes of this kind are germs, and many infections and diseases are caused by them.

clue.text: Offensive son, eager to learn about right, left separately

indicators.note: about means the eager word goes around the inserted letters
separately means the two letters go into the word at different points rather than together

parts.note: curious means eager to learn

explanation.surface: A rude, inquisitive boy keeps asking about right and left politics.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes in after CUR and L after the next I, giving CURRILOUS after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurrilous remarks are abusive and insulting, so offensive is a close synonym.

clue.text: Performer's assistant goes to pieces when given new order

indicators.note: the words, broken to pieces and put in a new order, become rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A magician's helper falls apart when told to do something different.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian's straight man or butt of jokes is called this, a supporting role to the main performer.

clue.text: Poet, otherwise sister to poet and painter

definitions.meaning: Christina, the Victorian writer of Goblin Market
Christina was sister to Dante Gabriel, the Pre-Raphaelite poet and painter

explanation.surface: A literary family puzzle: a poet who was also the sister of another poet-painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' links the two readings of the same surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the poet Christina and to her brother, the Pre-Raphaelite painter.

clue.text: American who had four sisters in family in rural cottage

definitions.text: American who had four sisters in family

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words rural cottage

explanation.surface: A large American family of sisters living in a country cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: Louisa May wrote Little Women about the four March sisters, modelled on her own family of four girls.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist Louisa May wrote Little Women, whose household is four sisters, drawn from her own girlhood.

clue.text: Humorous writer, tragic figure abused by children

definitions.meaning: Edward, the Victorian author of nonsense verse and limericks
Shakespeare's king who is cast out by his daughters Goneril and Regan

explanation.surface: A writer of comedy who became a tragic figure mistreated by his offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward wrote comic limericks, and Shakespeare's tragic king of that name is betrayed by his daughters.

clue.text: Poet and novelist whose father was a detective

definitions.text: Poet and novelist whose father was a detective

parts.words: Poet and novelist whose father was a detective
parts.note: G.K., the poet and novelist, created the priest-sleuth Father Brown; father is the clerical title, not a parent

explanation.surface: A writer whose dad worked as a police detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' suggests a parent; it is the priest Father Brown, the detective in G.K.'s stories.
explanation.definitionFit: G.K. wrote verse and novels, and his best-known creation is the clerical detective Father Brown.

clue.text: Brothers putting together macabre writing

parts.note: grim means macabre, ghastly
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Siblings collaborating on dark, gruesome stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob and Wilhelm were the German brothers who collected fairy tales, many of them macabre.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm, the fairy-tale collectors, are known collectively by their surname as the Brothers.

clue.text: Relatively small groups one newcomer upset in digs

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the word for digs

parts.note: mines are excavations, digs

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tiro is a beginner or newcomer

explanation.surface: Small groups of people disturbed by a new arrival in their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like British slang for lodgings; it is mines. 'upset' reverses I TIRO to ORITI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sections of a population that are smaller than the majority are called minorities, the plural of a lesser number.

clue.text: Mother dismissing the recorder of minutes for legal writer

indicators.note: dismissing means the following word is sent away from the letters of the first

parts.note: a timer records minutes passing; the secretary sense of minutes is a trick

explanation.surface: A mother sacks the minute-taker in favour of a lawyer who writes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder of minutes' suggests a secretary; it is a clock. John Mortimer was a barrister and author of the Rumpole stories.
explanation.definitionFit: John was a barrister who wrote the Rumpole of the Bailey courtroom stories, a writer on law.

clue.text: Novelist repeating conclusion reached by member of 22 across's family

indicators.note: repeating conclusion means the final letter of the family name is doubled

parts.note: the Bennets are the family of Pride and Prejudice by Austen, the answer to 22 across

explanation.surface: A writer mirroring the ending reached by a fictional family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold was the novelist of The Old Wives' Tale; the Austen family name gains one more T.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold, the Edwardian author of the Potteries books, was a prolific writer of fiction.

clue.text: In loving way, making proposal, with lady taking no notice

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer or proposal

indicators.note: taking no means the word for notice is removed from the following word

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A man proposes lovingly, but the lady pays him no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking no' removes AD from LADY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with gentle affection is acting lovingly, so the adverb fits the phrase.

clue.text: A book revised in new volume for son of Russian statesman

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters between the two abbreviations
a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A book reissued in a new edition for a Russian politician's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Vladimir, author of Lolita, was the son of the liberal statesman V.D. Nabokov.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir, the novelist of Lolita, was the son of a liberal politician of pre-revolutionary Russia.

clue.text: Singular craft seen in short humorous piece

parts.note: singular means one, single
a liner is an ocean-going craft, a ship

explanation.surface: A unique vessel appears in a brief comic sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip or joke delivered in a single sentence is a brief piece of humour.

clue.text: Clearly produces Hawaiian instrument or Japanese ornament

parts.note: to net is to clear as profit, so clearly produces means nets
uke is short for ukulele, the Hawaiian instrument

explanation.surface: Choosing between a Hawaiian guitar and a Japanese trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: A small carved toggle once worn on a kimono sash, now a collector's ornament from Japan.

clue.text: Source of novel combination of children and partners

definitions.text: Source of novel combination of children and partners

parts.words: Source of novel combination of children and partners
parts.note: D.H. wrote Sons and Lovers, a novel whose title joins children with partners

explanation.surface: Where a new arrangement of kids and spouses came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is a book, Sons and Lovers by D.H.
explanation.definitionFit: D.H. wrote Sons and Lovers, so he is the author behind a novel combining offspring and lovers.

clue.text: On vessel overseas with king going south

indicators.note: in a down clue, going south means the letter moves further down the word

parts.note: abroad means overseas
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king travels overseas and heads south on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship or other vessel means being on board, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Novelist finding little energy in dotty aunts

indicators.note: in places the energy letter inside the rearranged letters
dotty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy, a little of it

explanation.surface: A writer discovers her eccentric aunts have little energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' rearranges AUNTS to AUSTN, and E goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane, author of Emma and Pride and Prejudice, was a celebrated Regency writer of fiction.

clue.text: In a US city married undistinguished person

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
a married couple are made one

explanation.surface: In an American city, someone married a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Just any ordinary person, as in 'not just anybody', means someone of no distinction.

clue.text: He wrote about brothers in party changing votes — heavens!

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: changing means the letters of votes are rearranged

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: A writer at a party switches his votes and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges VOTES to STOEV. The Brothers Karamazov is Fyodor's last novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fyodor wrote The Brothers Karamazov, a novel about three siblings, so the clue describes him.

clue.text: Friends of French literary father and son

definitions.meaning: the author of Lucky Jim and his son Martin, novelist father and son

explanation.surface: French friends of a literary father and son.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plural for friends, and the surname shared by the Lucky Jim novelist and his son Martin.

clue.text: Fail as boy, being oddly deficient in addition

indicators.note: oddly deficient means the odd-numbered letters are missing, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A boy fails, being somewhat lacking as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means besides or as well, an everyday synonym for in addition.

clue.text: Etonian yearbook author whose elder sibling saw everything

definitions.text: Etonian yearbook author whose elder sibling saw everything

parts.words: Etonian yearbook author whose elder sibling saw everything
parts.note: the Old Etonian George wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four, a book titled by a year, where Big Brother watches all

explanation.surface: A schoolboy edited the Eton yearbook and had a nosy older brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yearbook' is a book named after a year, 1984, and the all-seeing elder sibling is Big Brother.
explanation.definitionFit: George went to Eton and wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four, whose watching dictator is called Big Brother.

clue.text: Martin's father, 19th-century novelist

definitions.meaning: the father of the novelist Martin Amis, himself the author of Lucky Jim
Charles, the Victorian author of The Water-Babies

explanation.surface: A modern writer's father was a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Martin Amis's father's first name and the surname of Charles, who wrote Westward Ho!
